content.text:
I've submitted **index 59** (Cr 0.10, Fe 0.32, V 0.58) as the best composition. It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.297%, but only by a hair over the next one.

I used all 3 merit measurements:

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 59 | 0.10 / 0.32 / 0.58 | 0.297 |
| 87 | 0.16 / 0.33 / 0.51 | 0.295 |
| 145 | 0.29 / 0.36 / 0.35 | 0.061 |

- **59 vs. 87:** the gap is tiny and likely within measurement noise, so these two are effectively tied.
- **Trend:** adding Cr and removing V clearly hurts. Index 145 came in about 5× lower than the other two. The better compositions sit in the vanadium-rich, low-chromium region, roughly around the (Fe,Cr)VO₄ ratio.
- **XRD (4 of 5 scans used):** indices 74, 87, 99 and 130 gave nearly identical patterns. XRD didn't separate the candidates, so I picked the EQE measurements on composition alone.

With only three measurements, I can't tell whether 59 is the library's true best. The obvious region I didn't test has even more vanadium and less chromium, such as indices 44 or 29. If more budget becomes available, measure there first.
